body.text: Victorians head to the polls today to decide who will lead the state for the next four years, as the leaders seek to make their final pitch to voters.
Opposition Leader Jess Wilson is attempting to unseat a 12-year-old Labor government, while Premier Ben Carroll is vying for a fourth term in office.
Follow our live coverage below.

Green surge coming, leader says
Greens leader Ellen Sandell says the mood is good at her constituents cast their votes in Kensington in her seat of Melbourne.
The party says it's confident of retaining the seats of Brunswick, Melbourne and Richmond, but is also hopeful of reclaiming Prahran, which it lost in a by-election in 2025.
It's also looking to take the seats of Northcote, Pascoe Vale, Preston and Footscray from Labor, after its candidates fell narrowly short of wins in 2022.
"We've know for months that there is a Greens surge coming and now we're seeing that play out in the polls," Sandell says.
"The fact that the Greens are even competive in seats that Labor has held for 99 years I think shows the extraordinary power of our movement."

She says Labor voters believe the party has abandoned its traditional values and she's accused the Liberal Party of being dishonest with the way its handled its announcement about privatising the sewerage system.
More pictures from Hanson's stop in Pakenham
Earlier we took you to Pakenham in Melbourne's outer south-east where One Nation's Victorian leader Warren Pickering is hoping to be voted into parliament.
One Nation is hoping it can win its first lower house seats in Victoria, with polls predicting the party could pick up 20 per cent of the vote across the state.
Pakenham residents are particularly worried about crime and the cost of living, and are experiencing high levels of mortgage stress.
Pickering caused a stir earlier in the campaign when he fronted a press conference and admitted drug and alcohol problems 20 years ago, in response to a newspaper report.
But it hasn’t seemed to do anything to dampen his popularity.
Pauline Hanson joined him in greeting voters and thanking party volunteers this morning.
Sitting Labor MP Emma Vulin holds the seat by a very narrow margin, but is retiring due to illness.
Polling suggests it will be a race between Mr Pickering and Liberal candidate Radmila Dyson, who is running in her first election.
Alessandra Soliven is the Labor candidate.
Voter Marcus says he's just voted for One Nation and is confident Pickering will win the seat.
"Just want things to change in Victoria," he says.
"Owning my own business, you really seeing what's going on lately, it's making it hard for small business owners."
Another voter wearing a One Nation cap says he's disappointed about the state of Victoria's economy and cost of living.
Premier casts his vote in Mebourne's north-west
Labor leader Ben Carroll has cast his vote at his old primary school of St Christopher's in Airport West.
Carroll has been vocal about growing up "under the flight path" as his father ran his own small business, and repeated the story to waiting media today.
He was accompanied by his wife Fiona and his young daughter.
Carroll waved to voters waiting in line in the school hall and stopped to talk to some constituents.
He says he's confident of Labor's chances.
"People do feel like they've been sold down the river by the Liberal Party," he says.
"After 50 per cent of Victorians had voted, to come out with a radical privatisation agenda around kinder, renewables and water. People do feel really angry about that."
He reminded the media that three months ago Liberal leader Jess Wilson said she did not have plans to privatise Melbourne Water.
📹 Watch Jess Wilson defend sewerage privatisation plan
Liberal leader Jess Wilson has told ABC Weekend Breakfast her plan to privatise the sewerage system will not lead to higher prices.
Greens looking to retain Melbourne
Voters are lining up to cast their ballots at the Melbourne Town Hall on a rainy and humid day in the city.
The CBD is part of the seat of Melbourne, held by Victorian Greens leader Ellen Sandell. She won the seat at the last election on a margin of more than 10 per cent.
Some polling suggests the Greens may increase their vote at today's state election.
The inner-city vibe did not deter a team of One Nation volunteers though. One of the volunteers in orange said he had travelled from South Australia to support the Victorian campaign.
Voter Zoe took her dog Gus along to the voting centre today.
She told the ABC she felt she "probably hadn't paid enough attention" during the election campaign.
"There's probably going to be a fairly big swing, so I just tried to make sure my vote didn't go anywhere I didn't want it to go, essentially," Zoe said.
Severe weather as Victorians head out to vote
The State Emergency Service has urged anyone "getting a democracy sausage or lamingtons to drive to the conditions of the area" after receiving more than 400 callouts for assistance in 24 hours.
Heavy rain and storms crossed the state overnight, with Maryborough, Bendigo and Ballarat the worst affected.
Of the 400 callouts, 105 were for fallen trees, 96 for building damage and some were for people driving through flood waters.
Powercor is reporting outages in Glenlyon, Daylesford and surrounds.
SES State Duty Officer Erin Mason told ABC Statewide Breakfast that rivers "responding to the rain that has fallen" were being monitored, including the Loddon River.
Intense rainfall and storms are expected to move across the north-east later today.
Victorian Coalition's election spending and saving explained ahead of state election
Liberal leader Jess Wilson rounds off her busy morning of television interviews with the ABC's Weekend Breakfast.
She again defends the late release of of the costings of the Liberal Party's plans for spending and savings.
The plan was the first time Victorians got a proper glimpse of the Coalition's plan to rein in government spending if it wins today's election.
Wilson defends the decision to release the numbers so late in the campaign, after roughly 2 million Victorians had already voted, saying it was up to them when they decided to head to the ballot box.
"These are the decisions that a responsible and disciplined government would make to repair the budget here in Victoria," she says.
She also says the privatisation of the sewerage system will not lead to higher prices.
"That's just a desperate scare campaign," she says. "The Essential Services Commission will continue to regulate water prices, as they do now."
The Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO) estimates the Coalition's policies will lower net debt by $20 billion over the next four years.
Take a read of the story from Stephanie Chalkley-Rhoden and Leanne Wong in the link below to see how the Coalition plans to do it.
One Nation has booted Labor from Victoria, Hanson says
One Nation leader Pauline Hanson is accompanying the party's Victorian leader Warren Pickering on a tour of Melbourne polling centres this morning.
Their first stop is Pakenham in the city's outer south-east, where Pickering is hoping to be elected.
It's one of the outer suburban seats, along with the likes of Melton and Sunbury, where One Nation could see some of its highest results.
"We know that Labor's out of the state. Finished," Hanson says.
"They won't be in government and that's where One Nation has played a big part in this. The Liberals could not have won it by themselves. No way in the wide world. We did the same in Queensland."
Pickering says he's feeling good about his chances.
"It's a consequence of knowing we put our best foot forward, we've left nothing on the table, there's nothing left in the tank, so now it's up to the people of Victoria," he says.
Jess Wilson defends late announcements
Liberal leader Jess Wilson has done consecutive television interviews this morning.
First up on Channel 9, she was asked about the release of her party's costings just two days before the election.

"We announced more than $26 billion of savings more than six months ago and this is about the final detail in terms of how we're going to repair the budget in this state," she said."We always said there would be more savings to come."
"We announced more than $26 billion of savings more than six months ago and this is about the final detail in terms of how we're going to repair the budget in this state," she said.
"We always said there would be more savings to come."
Wilson told Channel 7 she wasn't taking polls pointing towards a Liberal Party win for granted.
"I know there are a lot of polls, there are a lot of headlines but this election is going to be closer than what people think," she said.
She was also asked about her previous promise not to privatise the sewerage system.
"It doesn't touch the water coming out of your tap," she said. "It's a lease, not a sale."
One Nation texts voters vowing to fight Coalition's sewerage privatisation
As the campaign entered its final 24 hours, One Nation seized on the Coalition's controversial plan for a 90-year lease on Melbourne's sewerage system.
In text messages to voters on Friday, the party highlighted its intention to block the move.
It's a sign that at least one other party believes the policy — which the Coalition only revealed after 2 million people had cast early votes — is politically toxic.
Coalition to partly privatise Melbourne's sewerage network, cut level crossing removals
Just a two days out from the state election, Opposition Leader Jess Wilson released the Coalition's policy costings.
She revealed she would partly privatize Melbourne's sewerage network. In August, she said she "wouldn't touch" Melbourne Water if elected.
Wilson also announced the Coalition would axe and delay level crossing removals and put a halt on Labor's plans to expand free kindergarten if elected today.
The Parliamentary Budget Office estimates that the Coalition's policies lower net debt by $20 billion lower over four years to $176 billion.
For more details about what the Liberal leader unveiled on Thursday, read state political reporter Rachel Eddie's story below.
Don't forget your umbrella
There could be slower trade at the sausage sizzles and bake sales, as voters head out into a soggy day around the state.
Some areas received up to 100mm of rain over the past 24 hours, which has seen flash flooding in parts.
A Watch and Act alert for flash flooding remains for the town of Dunolly, north west of Melbourne, and parts of the Loddon River further west.
They're also warning of the potential for landslides and debris across roads.
A severe weather warning has also been issued for Victoria's North East and parts of Central, Gippsland, Northern Country and North Central districts.
Heavy rainfall and damaging winds are expected to develop in those areas today.
The SES has received more than 300 calls for help statewide.
When do polling booths close across Victoria?
Polling booths are open from 8am and close at 6pm today for the Victorian state election.
If you haven't voted yet and don't know where your nearest voting centre is, check out this link from the Victorian Electoral Commission.
We should start to get results filtering through some time after 6pm.
Welcome to our election blog 👋
Hello and welcome to our election live blog! It's democracy day here in Victoria and polling booths will be opening soon across the state.
Labor's Ben Carroll and Liberal leader Jess Wilson will make their final pitch to voters as we countdown the hours until polls close.

The Liberal leader is trying to unseat a 12-year-old Labor state government, while Carroll is attempting to win his party a historic fourth term in power. We'll have to wait to see what affect One Nation and the Greens will have on tonight's results.
Voting centres open at 8am across the state. We'll be here all day to bring you all the election day developments (and shenanigans!) as it happens.
So grab your democracy sausage and, if you haven't already, get out and vote! Join us for the rest of the day as we bring you election day live.
